episode_title: Ep 102: Stop Waiting for January: How to Make Q4 Count

real_qa.q: What should executives focus on in Q4 instead of waiting until January 2027 to set new goals?
real_qa.r: Rather than waiting for January, executives should pull out their existing year goals, identify the one or two actions that will create the most momentum in the next two weeks, and put those actions on their calendar immediately. The key is deciding what matters most and saying no to everything else. Q4 provides roughly 10 weeks of time to build real momentum and walk into 2027 already moving instead of starting from ground zero.

real_qa.q: How can executives stop being a single point of failure when their team keeps bringing them every problem?
real_qa.r: Instead of accepting or taking on the work when team members bring problems, ask them a simple question: What do you think the next step should be? This question pulls the team into ownership of the problem and solution. Once aligned on next steps, the leader can give the work away rather than accept it, keeping it with the rightful owner while maintaining discernment about when urgent situations truly require the leader to step in.
real_qa.requete: delegation question avoid single point failure

real_qa.q: What is the most effective approach for networking at large conferences with hundreds of attendees?
real_qa.r: Instead of trying to meet everyone at a large conference, set a clear goal in advance for who can help advance your long-term career goal. Use AI to filter through the attendee list and narrow it down to key people relevant to your goal. Connect with those people ahead of time before the event, so you arrive prepared. This approach transforms a 500-person conference into meaningful connections with exactly the right people, resulting in follow-up calls already scheduled.

real_qa.q: How should newly promoted executives handle self-doubt about whether their voice belongs in the C-suite?
real_qa.r: When imposter syndrome appears in a new executive role, work directly through that doubt and reconnect with the fact that you were hired for a reason. Remember who you are and the value you bring, and recognize that as a leader of your entire function and department, you are not a guest in the room—you are a member of the executive team. Trust your own strong intuition and lead authentically rather than trying to become someone you are not.
real_qa.requete: new executive imposter syndrome C-suite confidence

real_qa.q: How can job search resilience be maintained during an extended executive-level job hunt?
real_qa.r: When in a stressful job search, look back at a previous successful job search you have completed and ask yourself what you would tell your past self. The wisdom you gained from that experience is already within you—you just need the right question to access it. Coaching helps you reach the wisdom you already have by asking powerful questions rather than providing new tools or unsolicited advice.
